triage.evidence: Codex is right about the bytes: at dad3e7f5 specs/067-assurance-profiles/assurance.json has authority_snapshot and evidence_snapshot mode current, commit null (lines 15-108 and 112-115). That is the designed freeze model, not a defect. scripts/validate_spec_kit.py freeze() (:97-114) requires a clean candidate, takes commit = HEAD and writes mode historical with that commit into the working tree, so the record that names the candidate is necessarily committed after it; docs/development/SPEC_KIT.md (Assurance record: 'A reviewed candidate uses historical mode bound to a full Git commit whose authority bytes are verified from repository history'; evidence_snapshot 'permits a review to bind an earlier authority candidate while a later commit packages the review record') states the same. The freeze record is 906d2efd (#1403), whose only assurance.json change is the four freeze fields (both snapshots historical at dad3e7f5, authority hashes unchanged). 065 follows the same pattern (frozen at a768e6d3, recorded in 134a9731). Checked here: all 10 obtained_evidence sha256 in the develop assurance.json match the files at dad3e7f5, and all 89 authority_snapshot hashes match the bytes at dad3e7f5. The real, minor defect is the packet wording: review/codex-t011-20261116.md:11-14 says the snapshots are 'both historical at this commit', which is false for the candidate's own bytes and led Codex (prompt item 7) to this finding.
triage.reproduction: git show dad3e7f5:specs/067-assurance-profiles/assurance.json (current/null); git diff dad3e7f5 906d2efd -- specs/067-assurance-profiles/assurance.json (only commit and mode fields); sha256 of each obtained_evidence path and each authority path at dad3e7f5 against the develop record: 10/10 and 89/89 match.
triage.disposition: no change to the freeze; correct the packet sentence (candidate bytes are current, the historical binding lives in the later freeze commit) in the next packet revision

triage.evidence: verify_receipt (agent_braid/harness_assurance_receipts.py:287-306) takes the artifact from the caller; _row (:179-187) checks only the key set, schema, executionAuthorization false and the artifact's own digest (:184), and _verify_against (:309-322) then takes the effective depth and mode from that artifact's row; _check_mode (:253-266) compares with row mode only and has no independent floor check, although harness_assurance.HUMAN_ONLY (:68) and _check_checkpoint (:134) fix the floors. Anyone who can supply the artifact can re-seal it. The authoritative check exists (harness_assurance.verify_artifact :414-432, which recompiles and refuses with input-hash-mismatch) but verify_receipt neither calls it nor takes the inputs it needs, while its docstring (:7-9) and the contract (contracts/assurance-profile.md:79, 'profile binding') read as if the receipt were bound to the profile. Mitigation: there is no production caller of harness_assurance_receipts.verify_receipt in agent_braid/ or scripts/ (only tests), and the module docstring says a receipt is a record, not proof. The t011.json adversarial fixes (re-sealed artifact with emptied reviews refused) closed only the review-section variant.
triage.reproduction: In memory: compile the genuine artifact for agent_braid/cli.py, 500 lines (release human-only, pre-pr-review R3); re-seal a copy with release mode autonomous and pre-pr-review depth R0 with an empty required list. verify_artifact refuses it (input-hash-mismatch). verify_receipt accepts a release receipt with mode autonomous, author agent-x and no approval, and a pre-pr-review receipt at R0 with zero reviews. The same release receipt against the genuine artifact is refused (mode-below-effective). So a self-consistent, non-authoritative artifact makes a human-only floor pass with no human approval.
triage.disposition: fix before approval: verify_receipt must take the compilation inputs (profile, scope documents, classification) and call verify_artifact, or take an artifact the caller has verified and bind the receipt to its digest; independently refuse any HUMAN_ONLY checkpoint whose applied mode is not human-only with a human approval; add the negative control (valid digest, policy differs from the fresh compilation) and correct the contract's 'profile binding' wording

triage.evidence: compile_artifact (agent_braid/harness_assurance.py:389-411) applies the classification with apply_risk (:399) without re-evaluating the profile's riskRules against the classification's paths and changedLines; _check_consistency (agent_braid/harness_assurance_risk.py:143-162) checks only the fixed Q5 rules, and the classification carries no binding to the profile it was computed under. verify_artifact (:414-432) recompiles from the same stale classification and therefore agrees. This is distinct from the recorded caller-supplied impact residual (evidence/t011.json:31): no repository impact is needed to re-evaluate operator rules, since paths and changedLines are in the classification.
triage.reproduction: In memory: classify README.md, 10 lines under preset standard (no reasons); profile p3 = standard v2 plus rule readme-r3 (README.md, minChangedLines 0, raiseTo R3). Fresh classification under p3 raises to R3 and compiles at R3; compile_artifact(p3, None, stale) yields R2, and verify_artifact(that artifact, p3, None, stale) passes.
triage.disposition: fix before approval: in compile_artifact (and so verify_artifact) re-evaluate the profile's riskRules on the classification's paths and changedLines and refuse a classification whose operator reasons differ (invalid-diff-summary), or bind the classifying profile's digest into the classification; add the stale-classification negative control

triage.evidence: agent_braid/harness_assurance_risk.py:161-162 require only that a reason named size-over-400 or shared-file exists, not that it carries raiseTo R3 (DEFAULT_RAISE, :38). The test tests/test_harness_assurance_risk.py:222-231 uses agent_braid/harness_lab.py and agent_braid/cli.py, both sensitive paths, so the forged inputs keep a sensitive-path R3 reason while raiseDepthTo is reset to None and the generic max check at :158 refuses them; deleting either dedicated guard leaves the test passing. Lowered: it needs a forged classification, and a forger can already understate changedLines or paths (the recorded caller-supplied seam), so the guard is defense in depth; but t011.json credits these guards with tests ('tests added for hidden size and shared-file reasons').
triage.reproduction: In memory: docs/x.md, 401 lines under standard yields size-over-400 R3 (compile R3); the same classification with that reason at raiseTo R2 and raiseDepthTo R2 compiles at R2. ROADMAP.md (shared-file only) forged the same way compiles at R2. The test fixtures' reasons are [sensitive-path, size-over-400] and [sensitive-path, shared-file]; after the test's edit the remaining maximum is R3 against raiseDepthTo None, so the generic check alone refuses.
triage.disposition: fix in a follow-up task, recommended in the same fix PR as C67-002/C67-003 (one re-freeze): require the canonical R3 reason for each triggered Q5 default; rebuild the omission tests on non-sensitive paths (docs/x.md over 400 lines, ROADMAP.md) with consistent aggregates, and add the R2-raise variants

triage.evidence: Confirmed: _single_line (agent_braid/harness_assurance_render.py:80-85) admits any printable text up to 200 characters without Markdown syntax, and track_brief_section interpolates ownership, isolation, model and effort at :108-110, so '@' mentions and secret-like strings reach the brief. Not confirmed as a medium leak: the four fields are caller-supplied orchestrator metadata, not transcripts, and the renderer cannot recognise a secret in arbitrary text; '_' is refused (:28), which happens to stop some token formats (ghp_...) but not others (sk-ant-...). The @mention part is already recorded in evidence/t011.json:24 as low and deferred to a later task. The claim gap is real: assurance.json observation_contract ('No secret or raw transcript is exported.') is not enforced for these fields.
triage.reproduction: In memory: track_brief_section with ownership '@jayanez owns this', isolation 'token sk-ant-api03-ABCDEF0123456789' and effort 'user: paste of transcript line' renders all three verbatim; 'ghp_abc' and 'a|b' are refused (invalid-artifact).
triage.disposition: fix in a follow-up task: restrict the four fields to an identifier-like charset and refuse '@'; add synthetic-sensitive-text tests; narrow the observation_contract wording at the next re-freeze

triage.evidence: save_journal (agent_braid/harness_assurance.py:714-743) writes journal.to_bytes() without a size check, while read_operator_file (:464-489) refuses above MAX_BYTES 1048576 (agent_braid/system_one.py:17) with unobservable-source and ProfileJournal.from_bytes refuses it as invalid-json. MAX_PROFILES 64, MAX_RULES 16, MAX_PATTERNS 16 and MAX_PATTERN 128 allow valid journals above that cap. Lowered: it fails closed (the journal becomes unreadable, nothing is granted), needs about 30 human-committed maximal profile versions, and is an operator-only availability problem; the previous journal is overwritten, so recovery is manual.
triage.reproduction: In memory: ProfileJournal begin+commit by a human actor of standard-preset versions each with 16 rules of 16 patterns of 128 characters; after 30 versions (60 events) to_bytes() is 1084485 bytes (> 1048576) and ProfileJournal.from_bytes refuses it (invalid-json). No file was written.
triage.disposition: fix in a follow-up task: refuse in _append or save_journal (fixed reason, e.g. journal-full) when the canonical bytes would exceed MAX_BYTES, keeping the previous file; add a boundary test
